content.title: CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE JADEN IVEY AND MIKE CONLEY JR. IN THREE-TEAM TRADE | Chicago Bulls
content.text: The Chicago Bulls announced today the team has acquired guard Jaden Ivey along with guard Mike Conley Jr. in a three-team deal involving the Detroit Pistons and Minnesota Timberwolves. Chicago dealt forward Kevin Huerter and center Dario Šarić to the Pistons as part of the trade.Ivey, 6-3, 195, arrives in Chicago currently in his fourth NBA season with career averages of 14.9 points (.431 FG%, .354 3FG%), 3.5 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 27.9 minutes through 214 games (166 starts) with Detroit. Ivey averaged at least 15.0 points in each of his first three NBA seasons, including career highs of 17.6 points (.460 FG%, .409 3FG%) and 4.1 rebounds to go along with 4.0 assists in 2024-25.The former Purdue product was drafted fifth overall by the Pistons in the 2022 NBA Draft, earning NBA All-Rookie Second-Team honors with averages of 16.3 points and 5.2 assists through 74 games (73 starts). In a career-high 77 games (61 starts) the following season, Ivey had 17 games with 20-plus points and four games with 30-plus points in 2023-24, including a career-high 37 points at the Sacramento Kings on Feb. 7, 2024. Ivey has totaled 43 games scoring at least 20 points and seven games eclipsing 30 points during his career.The South Bend, Ind. native has appeared in 33 games (two starts) with the Pistons this season, averaging 8.2 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 16.8 minutes, while logging 12 games with 10-plus points and 14 games with multiple three-pointers made. A consensus All-America Second Team selection and All-Big Ten First Team honoree in 2021-22, Ivey was the highest drafted player out of Purdue since 1994 (Glenn Robinson).Conley Jr., 6-1, 175, holds career averages of 13.7 points, 2.9 rebounds and 5.6 assists in 30.8 minutes through 1,216 games (1,137 starts) with the Minnesota Timberwolves (2023-26), Utah Jazz (2019-23) and Memphis Grizzlies (2007-19). Conley Jr. ranks 25th in NBA history in total assists (6,751), 23rd all-time in three-pointers made (1,972) and 30th among all NBA players in career steals (1,629). He is one of 14 players in NBA history with at least 16,000 points, 6,000 assists and 1,600 steals.The Fayetteville, Ark. native has appeared in 44 games (nine starts) this season with Minnesota, averaging 4.4 points, 1.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 18.5 minutes. Now in his 19th NBA season, Conley Jr. was an NBA All-Star in 2020-21 and earned NBA All-Defensive Second Team honors in 2012-13. He ranks first all-time in Grizzlies history in total points (11,733), assists (4,509), steals (1,161) and three-pointers made (1,086), while also being named a four-time Joe Dumars Trophy Sportsmanship Award winner (2014, 2016, 2019, 2023) and a two-time Twyman-Stokes Teammate of the Year selection (2019, 2024).Huerter appeared in 70 games (27 starts) for Chicago and averaged 11.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.8 assists in 26.0 minutes. During the 2025-26 season, Huerter saw action in 44 games (11 starts) and posted averages of 10.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists.Šarić appeared in five games during the 2025-26 season with the Sacramento Kings. He was acquired via a three-team trade involving the Kings and Cleveland Cavaliers on Feb. 1.Chicago now has 17 rostered players, including two two-way contracts (Yuki Kawamura, Lachlan Olbrich).
